RULE-1.gloss: If John has l lego sets and the price per lego set is p, then the lego revenue is 195
RULE-1.formula: ∀l∀p((LegoSets(john, l) ∧ LegoSetPrice(p)) → RevenueLego(john, l, p, n_195))
RULE-1.verify_reason: encodes lego revenue as a fixed 195 rather than a general l*p relation

RULE-2.gloss: If John buys g video games at price q, then the video game cost is 160
RULE-2.formula: ∀g∀q((VideoGamesBought(john, g) ∧ VideoGamePrice(q)) → CostVideoGames(john, g, q, n_160))
RULE-2.verify_reason: encodes video game cost as fixed 160 instead of g*q

RULE-3.gloss: If revenue from lego sales is 195 and cost of video games is 160, then remaining money is 35
RULE-3.formula: ∀l∀p∀g∀q((RevenueLego(john, l, p, n_195) ∧ CostVideoGames(john, g, q, n_160)) → RemainingMoney(john, n_195, n_160, n_35))
RULE-3.verify_reason: encodes remaining money as fixed 35 given 195 and 160; uses embedded arithmetic

RULE-4.gloss: If leftover money is 5 and remaining money is 35, then there is a discrepancy
RULE-4.formula: ∀j((LeftoverMoney(john, n_5) ∧ RemainingMoney(john, n_195, n_160, n_35)) → Discrepancy(john, n_35, n_5))
RULE-4.verify_reason: a reasonable consistency-check rule; if both leftover money values hold, then a discrepancy

INF-1.gloss: RevenueLego(john, n_13, n_15, n_195) from FACT-1 and FACT-2 by RULE-1 (Modus Ponens)

INF-2.gloss: CostVideoGames(john, n_8, n_20, n_160) from FACT-3 and FACT-4 by RULE-2 (Modus Ponens)

INF-3.gloss: RemainingMoney(john, n_195, n_160, n_35) from INF-1 and INF-2 by RULE-3 (Conjunction + Modus Ponens)

INF-4.gloss: Discrepancy(john, n_35, n_5) from INF-3 and FACT-5 by RULE-4 (Modus Ponens)
